**Ask which ordering carries information before deciding what to shuffle.** In a stateful RNN, the hidden state from one chunk may initialize the next chunk of the same sequence. Randomly placing an unrelated chunk next would attach the wrong history to its inputs. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

An online-learning simulation also needs chronological processing: the model at time t must not have learned from observations arriving later. A deliberate curriculum has an intended order that arbitrary shuffling would undo.

**Independent time-series windows are different.** If each example contains its own complete historical window, labels are correctly aligned, and hidden state resets between examples, training windows can often be shuffled safely. The order inside each window and the chronological train/test boundary still matter.

Separate three decisions: order within an example, order across stateful batches, and order among independent examples. “Never shuffle time series” confuses them. Test the data pipeline with known sequence IDs and timestamps so hidden-state carryover or future availability does not become an invisible source of leakage.

**Technical details and references.**

Do not arbitrarily reorder chunks when hidden state is carried from one chunk to the next, or when an online learner must simulate chronological availability. A deliberate curriculum also has an intended order. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

However, time-series **training windows** can often be shuffled if each window is self-contained, hidden state is reset correctly, and train/validation splits remain chronological. “Never shuffle time series” is therefore too broad. Separate the ordering needed inside an example, across stateful batches, and between independent examples. Check labels and timestamps before deciding the sampling policy.
